prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle graphene, opening the field of moire quantum matter.

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene remains my first choice. It is a rare sequence in which a concrete, quantitative theoretical prediction (the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model of 2011) was followed seven years later by an experiment that found correlated insulators and superconductivity at exactly the predicted regime. Five of eight members place it in their top three and all eight rank it, which is unusually broad, but I weigh it on the science: it gave condensed matter a platform where interaction strength is tuned by geometry and gate voltage, and it has been independently reproduced and extended to twisted multilayers, TMDs and fractional Chern insulators. In my opening I proposed only MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero. After reading the ballots I now favour naming Bistritzer as well. Four colleagues (Danielsson, Eriksson, Pearce, Olsson) name him, and the continuum-model paper is a joint Bistritzer-MacDonald result, so a citation for the prediction that omits him would be hard to defend. This keeps the prize at three people, with the theory pair and the leader of the experimental discovery.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservations are about maturity and attribution. The origin of superconductivity in magic-angle graphene is unresolved, and many correlated phases are still debated, so recognising the field now could look early if the mechanism turns out to be different from what the community assumes. On attribution, the experimental discovery was a group effort (Cao, Fatemi and colleagues, with Jarillo-Herrero as the leader), and other groups (Dean, Efetov, Young, Yazdani) did important confirming work, so a three-name limit cannot do justice to the whole field. The prediction also had precursors in earlier work on twisted graphene layers, which the committee would need to weigh.

responses.point: Kroll ranks the optical lattice clock first because it is a clean invention that changed what can be measured, and he places B001 fourth because the superconducting state is not settled and recognition may be somewhat early.
responses.response: I agree that B007 is the cleanest attribution on the list and that the metrology case is strong; it is my first alternative. But I do not think an open mechanism for the superconductivity weakens B001 as a discovery. The discovery is the flat-band prediction and the observation of correlated and superconducting states, which are not in dispute and have been reproduced by many groups. Waiting for a mechanism would be a stricter standard than the committee has applied to other experimental discoveries. I also note that Kroll himself counts the redefinition of the second as still pending, which is a similar kind of open maturity point for B007, so I do not see it as a decisive difference in favour of the clock.

responses.point: Johansson ranks circuit QED first and declares his own field proximity (superconducting circuits), noting that the supplied names omit Andreas Wallraff and that the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is closely related.
responses.response: I appreciate the disclosure of field proximity and the effort to judge strictly on the merits; I would still ask the rest of us to weigh B058 on the evidence rather than on that ranking alone. Johansson's own attribution point is also a real problem: if Wallraff's experimental role was central, the supplied three names do not describe the discovery, and a three-person limit makes that difficult to repair. The closeness to the 2025 prize on circuit-based quantum tunnelling adds a second obstacle. For these reasons I rank B058 below B001 and B007, although I accept that its impact on quantum technology is very large.

responses.point: Pearce supports B001 first, with a clean theory-plus-experiment configuration of MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer, and places the IceCube neutrino discovery second as an experimentalist, while doubting Spiering's role.
responses.response: I agree with Pearce on the three-name configuration for B001 and have moved to it from my two-name opening. On B039 I would be cautious: the diffuse flux is solid, but the source associations are at a few-sigma level and the allocation within a very large collaboration is as hard as Pearce says. Dropping Spiering would leave Halzen and Karle, which is defensible, but I would not put it ahead of the clock or the atom-lattice work on attribution grounds.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks the clock first and B001 fourth, saying the interpretation of the correlated states is not fully stable and recognition may be somewhat early, and she prefers Cirac and Zoller second.
responses.response: I do not agree that the interpretation is unstable in the sense that matters. The disputed point is the pairing mechanism, while the existence of flat-band correlated insulators and superconductivity is robust. I accept her point that B015 is conceptually deep, but Cirac and Zoller are theory proposals whose experimental realisation is credited to other groups, and Zoller also appears in B008. I would rather not spend one of three places on a theory-only prize while an entry with a prediction and its discovery is available.

uncertainties: Whether the committee should name Bistritzer, or a different experimental co-author, alongside MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero given the three-person limit.
How much weight to give the unresolved origin of superconductivity when judging whether recognition is timely.
Whether the optical lattice clock (B007) should be preferred because of its cleaner attribution and mature, reproduced performance.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile. My own research on active matter and statistical physics is not part of any shortlisted entry, and I have no documented connection to the candidates in B001, B007 or B008. Johansson has disclosed field proximity to B058, which I note for the committee.
